title: Two-step monodromy of special quasi-projective varieties

issues.description: Theorem 1.1 rests on the claim that CDY Lemma 4.4 and Proposition 4.13 give the full ordinary exact sequence pi1(F) -> pi1(V0) -> pi1(Alb V0) -> 1 for every special V0, together with dominance and a connected general fibre. The CDY paper was not available locally, so this input could not be checked against the source. The internal argument is correct once the input is granted.
issues.evidence: By Lemma 4.4 and Proposition 4.13, the algebraic quasi-Albanese map of a smooth special quasi-projective variety is dominant, has connected general fibre, and has the ordinary exact sequence (1.1).

coverage: Read in full: introduction.tex, mhs.tex (proof of Theorem 1.2), linear.tex (Theorem 1.1 and the log-Kodaira-zero corollary), specialness.tex and albanese-topology.tex (Theorem 1.3), plus INPUTS.md and dependencies.mmd. Checked step by step: (1) the Fujino H1 isomorphism gives [Gamma,Gamma] in N with finite quotient, so k_c=[g_c,g_c]; (2) gamma_r g_c has weights <= -r, so B_c=k_c/[k_c,k_c] has weights <= -2, while it is a quotient of H_1(F), which has weights >= -2, so B_c is pure of weight -2 by strictness; (3) g_c tensor k_c has weights <= -3, so [g,k] lies in [k,k], hence gamma3 = gamma4 = 0 by nilpotence; (4) the inverse-limit and base-change steps. For the example I checked by hand: K_Y+D = (n-2) times the pullback of a P1-point class (log Kodaira dimension 1); D_i.A_j = delta_ij, so there are no units and the quasi-Albanese is E; the meridian discs through the retained A_i give pi1 = Z^2; the curve-base argument via complete elliptic slices and orbifold Riemann-Hurwitz; and the bound on sections for a surface base. I skimmed definitions.tex, composition.tex and ordinary.tex but did not check them in detail. I did not check the claimed error in CDHP Claim 7.17 against CDHP itself.
main_claim: For a connected smooth special complex quasi-projective variety, every complex linear representation of pi1 has a virtually class-at-most-two nilpotent image. This follows from a completion theorem: if the quasi-Albanese map is dominant and the fibre-to-total-to-base pi1 sequence is exact, the rational unipotent completion is finite-dimensional of class at most two. The paper also gives special open surfaces (blowups of E x P1 minus horizontal curves) whose general quasi-Albanese fibre is not special.
